1  HON'BLE VIKAS BUDHWAR, J. 
1. Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Virendra Singh Patel, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Pankaj Kumar Rai,
learned State Law Officer for the State.

3. This application u/s 528 of BNSS has been preferred to quash the summoning order dated 19-04-2019 passed in Complaint Case No.94/2018 (Smt.Kranti Vs. Awdhesh and others) U/s 498A,
323, 506 of the I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S.-Erich, District-Jhansi, pending before the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Garautha, District-Jhansi.

sentences.text:
4. The case of applicants is that a complaint was lodged by the opposite party no. 2 on 11.07.2018 against the applicants who happens to be father-in-law, mother-in-law and husband and others under Sections, 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC read with Section 3/4 of the DP Act with an allegation that the marriage of the opposite party no. 2 stood solemnized with Awadhesh on 01.07.2014, however,
in the marriage gifts worth lacks of rupees were offered and huge expenditure was also incurred but the applicants being father-in-law and mother-in-law along with the husband and other family members were not satisfied with the gifts so offered and their demand was much more pursuant whereto the applicants were assaulted, maltreated and all sorts of harassment were being extended and the demand was of a motorcycle and 50,000/- cash.

Thereafter, post tendering of good offices, a settlement stood arrived on 26.11.2016, however, on 01.06.2018, the opposite party no. 2 was assaulted, she was thrown out from matrimonial house and was inflicted beating and all sorts of harassment were made pursuant whereto a registered complaint was lodged on 21.06.2018 and the complaint dated 11.07.2018.

Post recording of the statement of complainant under Section 200 followed by of Om Prakash under Section 202, Ram Lal, the applicants came to be summoned on 19.04.2019 under Sections 498, 323, 506 IPC read with Section 3/4 of the DP Act.
5. Questioning the summoning order, the present application has been filed.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that the summoning order cannot be sustained for the simple reason that only general and omnibus allegations have been levelled without there being any specific date or instances when the demand of dowry was made.

Though the applicants have been summoned under Section 323 but there is no injury report available on record and further a false and a concocted story has been cooked up that demand of dowry was being made.

It is also contended that the statements of the witnesses under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. are tailor-made just in order to suit the circumstances of the prosecution and the applicants have been summoned in a routine manner without recording any prima facie satisfaction about the application of the penal sections.

He also submits that the husband of the opposite party no2. and the son of the applicants went missing pursuant whereto the proceedings are lingering on and further the applicants have also obtained bail.

Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants shall be preferring discharge application Kamta Prasad And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114791787/
2 7.

sentences.text:
Learned AGA, on the other hand, submits that from the perusal of the allegations contained in the complaint vis-a-vis the statements under Section 200 and 202 of the Cr.P.C., offences are made out and the court below has meticulously analyzed the statements and their allegations and proceeded to record satisfaction.
8.
I heard the submissions so made across the bar and perused the record carefully.

9. Considering the submissions so made across the bar as well as the stand of the counsel for the applicant as per instructions received from appellant and the nature of allegations as well as overall fact situation, the application stands disposed of granting liberty to the applicants to prefer discharge application by 26.09.2025 and on the said motion, the court below shall decide the same strictly in accordance with law without granting unnecessary delay.

10. Till the discharge application is decided, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in summoning order dated 19-04-2019 passed in Complaint Case No.94/2018 (Smt.Kranti Vs.
Awdhesh and others) U/s 498A, 323, 506 of the I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
P.S.-Erich, District-Jhansi, pending before the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Garautha, District-Jhansi.
11.
